notes.body: The song counts a week night by night, each one a different stage of the same relationship. The count picks up again in the second verse and runs past seven.

notes.title: SZA
notes.body: The R&B singer whose 2017 debut album Ctrl includes the hit that names the third night. Her music is what's playing.

notes.title: Chevrolet Impala
notes.body: Chevy's long-running full-size sedan, a favorite for lowriders.
She tells him not to worry about a guy she swears is only a friend, and he learns better. Once he's gone, his phone gets quieter, and he counts that as a win.
Seven nights aren't enough, so he calls for an eighth. Then he plays week against weak: a week only holds seven days, and that's the problem.
The hook pairs racing through cars on the road with a feeling that won't wear off. He's weaving toward someone, and what stays with him is how love smells.

notes.title: Love Lockdown
notes.body: Kanye West's 2008 single from 808s & Heartbreak, an album built on the Roland 808 drum machine. He names the song and the machine in a few words.

notes.title: Madden NFL
notes.body: EA Sports' long-running football video game. Her games are maddening, and Madden is where you call the plays.

notes.title: Beyblade
notes.body: The spinning-top toy and anime, where tops are launched with a ripcord and a shout to let it rip. He starts things right away, the same way.

notes.title: Major Payne
notes.body: Damon Wayans' 1995 comedy about a hard-nosed Marine put in charge of a group of young cadets. Calling her to attention is his move.
He won't say who he's really after, only how many letters are in her name, and then he pretends not to know the count. It's a playful dodge at the end of a song that never sits still.

notes.title: Violet and Tate
notes.body: The doomed teen couple from the first season of American Horror Story, played by Taissa Farmiga and Evan Peters. Their romance never leaves one haunted house, which is why his never goes out on dates.
The verse plays like a scene: he's been on the road for hours, he's hungry, she has to let him in, and they race to her door. He wins. Small moments at home are the whole relationship.

notes.title: Gary Payton
notes.body: The Hall of Fame point guard nicknamed The Glove for his smothering defense with the Seattle SuperSonics. She fits him the way the nickname fit Payton.

Leaving turns into a fight: she grills him, his keys vanish, and he's sure she's behind it. When he finally gets out, he says he might as well disappear, which is exactly the show's rule: its ghosts can't exist anywhere outside that house.

He opens with a warning that this is as exposed as he gets. Then come the details that make it real: the post that tells him she's over it, and the song they shared still playing every time his phone rings.

notes.title: Kevin Durant
notes.body: The scoring great who has worn number 35 for most of his career, respected for a jumper almost no one can guard. Taking his chance with a woman earns him the same respect.

notes.title: Hermès Birkin
notes.body: Hermès's handbag, one of the most expensive and hardest to get in fashion. She wants one while an older man's money comes from the stock market.
He can't get an apology, can't stop checking her Instagram, and hears she's doing great on her own. Then he lands on the idea that gives the EP its name: getting better is painful in its own right.
